items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And we became dear friends. And I used him on any T.V. or movie session I could get him on.

ctx.x: On the, talk about Steely Dan for a bit. On the one side of the Aja LP you have Tom Scott on “Black Cow,” you have Pete Christlieb on “Deacon Blues” and you’ve got Wayne Shorter. You couldn’t get anybody good, could they?

I know. Pete Christlieb is another one I should have included him in that list of people I mentioned. Pete I met when I was about 14 years old. There was a youth band initiated by Ollie Mitchell, who was a great trumpet player. He was a studio trumpet player back in those days and they had a rehearsal facility and I wanted to join the band so badly. So I walk in the door and then there’s this tall, I don’t know I was 14 maybe he was 16 I don’t know, maybe like that. And he’s playing this fantastic solo. And I go…
At what point in Steely Dan recordings did you get the tunes that you were going to add horn section parts to?
